title: Converge affinity routing and cache staleness sanitizer
creator: Elena Park
description: Consolidate routing affinity heuristics (region/tenant/model affinity) with a lightweight cache-staleness sanitizer to reduce hotkey-induced tail latency and redundant model loads. Current behavior: multiple routing layers apply separate affinity rules, causing churn in slot allocation and KV cache thrashing when session affinities conflict. This ticket refactors the routing decision pipeline to a single affinity resolver, introduces a sanitizer that detects and refreshes potentially stale KV entries without full eviction, and adds observability around affinity flip rates. The change aims to lower p99 latency for short-lived chat sessions and reduce unnecessary model variant swaps under bursty traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity resolver removes duplicate/conflicting routing rules and exposes a single deterministic policy for routing decisions
Sanitizer reduces full KV eviction events by >= 60% on synthetic hotkey workload compared to baseline
End-to-end p99 latency improvement of at least 8% on short sessions workload in staging cluster
New metrics emitted: affinity_resolution_latency, affinity_flip_rate, kv_sanitize_attempts, kv_sanitize_success
Automated integration tests covering sanitization success/failure modes and fallback to safe-evict path
Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime/infra leads and SRE; PR(s) merged with green CI
design_notes: Introduce AffinityResolver component that consumes: request headers, tenant policy, model variant hints, and slot topology snapshot. Resolver returns a ranked list of candidate targets and an affinity score.

Sanitizer operates as a non-blocking, best-effort background step: it checks KV entry TTL, last-access epoch, and a cheap hash to detect staleness; it performs lightweight rehydration (refresh metadata, extend lease) before doing any heavy-weight eviction/rehash.
Avoid centralized locking: sanitizer uses compare-and-swap on KV metadata version and records attempted sequence numbers to prevent thundering rehydrates.
Trade-offs: stricter affinity consistency would require global lease renewals and hurt throughput; we prioritize probabilistic sanitizer with metrics and fallbacks to ensure availability.
Compatibility: resolver API is backward-compatible with current router; we add an opt-in feature flag for rollout. No changes required in client RPC surface.
Observability: emit emitted metrics at 10s rollup, add dashboard stub in Console to visualize affinity_flip_rate and kv_sanitize_success across models and regions.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype AffinityResolver and wire into router decision path behind feature flag; add unit tests for ranking logic (Mateo)
Week 2: Implement KVStalenessSanitizer as background actor with safe rehydrate flow; add local integration tests and add metrics (Anika)
Week 3: End-to-end staging run with synthetic hotkey and short-session traces; tune sanitizer thresholds, add dashboards (SRE + Observability)
Week 4: Gradual canary rollout to 10% of ingress traffic with auto-rollback on increased error/p99; capture telemetry for 72h, iterate; full rollout after validation
risks_mitigation: Risk: Sanitizer could under- or over-correct and cause extra write amplification. Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and a dry-run mode that records intended actions without applying them.
Risk: Resolver ranking bugs could route to incompatible model variants. Mitigation: resolver will verify compatibility matrix before selecting; add unit tests and runtime assertion hooks.

Risk: Rollout regressions affecting latency. Mitigation: gradual rollout with canary alarms (p50/p95/p99, error rate, model-swap frequency) and automatic rollback policy tied to existing release tooling.
Operational: Increase in metric cardinality. Mitigation: roll up labels (region/model_family) and keep tag set bounded; add retention policy to Console dashboard.
Dependency risk: this work touches slot allocator snapshot API; coordinate dependency upgrade window with ENG-30712 to avoid merge conflicts.
test_plan: Unit tests for AffinityResolver ranking under various policy permutations
Property tests for KVStalenessSanitizer compare-and-swap flows and no-op dry-run path
Staging benchmark using hotkey generator (see playbook link) to measure eviction counts and p99 latency before/after
Chaos test: simulate rapid tenant policy flips and validate sanitizer does not block serving; assert no increase in 5xx
Integration tests verifying metrics are emitted and dashboard panels load without cardinality explosion

2025-02-14: AffinityResolver prototype wired into router behind feature flag. Local unit tests passing. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123

2025-02-16: KVStalenessSanitizer actor implementation 60% complete; added metrics kv_sanitize_attempts and kv_sanitize_success. Bench harness for hotkey workload ready in staging. Mateo running initial perf sweep.
2025-02-18: First staging run shows 45% reduction in full-evict events with conservative sanitizer settings; p99 improved ~4%. Need further tuning to hit acceptance delta. Open questions noted below.
open_questions: What is the acceptable sanitizer error budget (false positives vs false negatives) for Tier A customers? Consult Product on SLAs before final thresholds.
Should affinity_resolution_latency be included in per-request traces by default or behind a sampling flag? Observability trade-offs exist.
Does any existing downstream component rely on the prior multi-step routing side-effects? Need to run a dependency grep across infra repos to find callers.
Is there an opportunity to reuse existing lease-renewal background job rather than new actor? Performance implications to be assessed.
